title: Loan Approval System Has an Inverted Debt-to-Income Ratio
description:
A loan-approval system spanning 5 files across 4 layers (models, repository, loan rules, service, route handler). `is_approved(applicant)` should approve a loan only if **all** of: credit score is at least 650, debt-to-income ratio is 0.4 or below, and employment is verified. Right now well-qualified applicants are getting denied, and `active_loans_count` is being bumped for applicants whose loans were denied. There are **multiple bugs across different files**. Trace the whole flow (`routes.py` -> `loan_service.py` -> `loan_rules.py`) before changing anything.

**Entry point**
`handle_loan_request(applicant_id, application_id, requested_amount, repository) -> dict`

**Approval rule**
Approved only if `credit_score >= 650` AND `existing_debt / annual_income <= 0.4` AND `employment_verified`. `active_loans_count` should only increment for applicants whose loan is actually approved.
